Jobs, fellowships, courses and calls

Jagiellonian University seeks a postdoctoral researcher for its South Indian song cultures project

The two-year research post in Kraków belongs to VOICES, a European Research Council project on the pattu song traditions of South India. Applications close on 21 November 2026.

Talaash Heritage desk · Published 9 November 2026

Where
Kraków, Poland
Apply by
21 November 2026

The Jagiellonian University in Kraków, Poland, is recruiting one assistant professor on the research staff (a postdoctoral post) for VOICES, a project funded by the European Research Council. The post sits in the university's Centre for Comparative Studies of Civilisations, in the Faculty of Philosophy. The selection notice was issued on 30 October 2026, and the project's principal investigator, Cezary Galewicz, shared it on the INDOLOGY mailing list on 8 November.

The project, titled 'Voices from the Deep South: the rise of Pattu song cultures of South Asia', traces how South India's song traditions developed before and during colonial rule. In Malayalam, pattu means song. The project notes that Kerala alone has close to eighty song genres, many tied to ritual occasions, and it plans a digital archive mapping songs across South India.

Candidates need a PhD or equivalent in Asian studies, Indology, anthropology, religious studies, ethnomusicology or a closely related field, and expert command of at least one South Indian language, with Malayalam preferred. They should also have research experience, in Asian contexts, in at least one of: oral literature and folklore; traditional music and dance; ritual, performance and festivals; religion and possession; or the body and embodiment. They also need a publication record and strong English. Digital humanities and audiovisual skills are welcome but not required.

The full-time contract runs for two years and may be extended by two more, with a start expected in the first quarter of 2027. The notice gives a basic gross pay range of PLN 16,850 to 20,200, and says the university does not provide housing.

Applications, including a CV, the university's personal questionnaire and declarations, a copy of the doctoral diploma and a statement of achievements, go by email to erc.voices@uj.edu.pl, with the subject line the notice specifies, by 21 November 2026. The university expects to settle the selection by 7 December 2026.
